scope: Durable shared vanilla/React SDK ownership, explicit failed-close recovery, permanent shutdown fencing and retained unsaved journals during database upgrade. Existing original Rust document, command, ABI and journal protocols are unchanged.

ownership.startup: Claim one host, await shared runtime initialization, compile the original configured standard profile, acquire the origin-wide room/writer lease, restore the exact saved journal or create the first seed, complete its initial local save and mount a DOM coordinator borrowing that session's core.
ownership.seedPolicy: Existing journals take precedence over document/frame/checkpoint/empty initial values. Fresh empty writers receive a native-admitted caret before their first save. Profile objects are freed after create/restore callbacks finish; the owner retains its codec.
ownership.cancellation: An individual aborted runtime wait does not cancel another consumer's initialization. Late storage/factory results close safely before a failed opening returns. Original host nodes are restored; a failed cleanup hands off an exact checkpoint/close/discard recovery capability.
ownership.close: UI and borrowed adapters stop before permanent coordinator retirement. No subsequent local or remote publication is admitted, including previously held queued frames. The exact checkpoint remains readable until its completed IndexedDB transaction and writer release.
ownership.failure: A rejected close retains the retired native owner and exclusive writer lease for export and close retry. It does not silently discard state or reopen authoring. Explicit discard waits for an already-started transaction before releasing the writer and never deletes the stored journal.
ownership.versionChange: A database upgrade closes its old connection and retires publication but keeps an unsaved native journal and lease. The application can export it, explicitly discard and restore into an admitted store. No unfamiliar database version is overwritten.
ownership.react: React never reconciles editable children. Parent renders update callbacks without replacing native history; key changes serialize durable old close before new opening. StrictMode, unmount, late startup and failed retirement are covered. onCloseError is required, including for failed startup cleanup and after unmount.
ownership.domCompatibility: Low-level SharedDomEditor still transfers core ownership by default. Session-managed mounts explicitly use coreOwnership borrow. A transferred owner is also freed when new queue-option admission rejects; an already-owned raw object is never freed by a rejected second transfer.

unitChecks.proof: Runtime/host/local React regressions plus durable session coordination, queued retirement, duplicate ownership, pending transaction ordering, explicit discard, failed-close retry, version-change retention, shared React serial lifetime and headless startup recovery. These unit tests use controlled fake owners/storage; installed browser tests below use the actual packaged Rust/Wasm owner and IndexedDB/Web Locks.

limits: The first-two-workstream goal is still active. Structural blocks/tasks, broader selection/navigation, natural typing groups, live read-only mode and bounded block properties/context UI remain open; retirement is not read-only editing.

Public profile/API/package and registry crate publishing decisions, remaining rich source promotion and separate sanitized HTML/Markdown/Office interchange remain work. All thirteen V1 qualification gates stay open.

Autosave is not abrupt-process-exit durability, a server acknowledgement or an asset-byte backup. Applications own transport/authentication, separate asset storage, recovery handoff and explicit discard decisions.
SSR is an inert starting placeholder, not a static document renderer. Broader framework adapters remain open.

Browser automation keys and clipboard-event payloads do not qualify physical native clipboard, IME, VoiceOver, historical WebKit repair, supported mobile or measured performance. Those later checks were not attempted.
